column1: # tests/math/long_double_cases.tsv - M142. What each long double function in
# One row per `long double` (or long/long long/int of a long double)
# declaration in that header, and tools/math-long-double-test.sh fails if a
# declaration has no row here, for the reason tests/math/cases.tsv gives: a
# libm function nobody grades is the shape these files exist to prevent.
# The answer comes from MPFR, through GCC. Every expected value in the
# generated table is a `__builtin_<name>l(...)` call on constant arguments,
# which GCC folds at COMPILE time using MPFR at this target's own 64-bit
# mantissa - so the oracle is a library nobody here wrote, evaluating at the
# precision under test, and the test asserts the generated object references
# no math symbol at all. A value that failed to fold would have been computed
# by the implementation under test at run time, which is the one outcome that
# would make the whole instrument vacuous.
# kind  1  one argument, swept over [lo, hi]
#       L  one argument, swept over [lo, hi] in the EXPONENT - log spacing,
#          which is the only useful sweep for exp and log
#       E  one argument, lo + (hi - lo) * 2^-k - the sweep that reaches
#          a function's domain edge, which a linear one never gets near
#       2  two arguments, swept over the grid pairwise
#       P  two arguments, the pow grid: base log-spaced, exponent linear
#       i  returns an integer type; compared EXACTLY, no tolerance
#       -  not graded by the swept table; the note says what grades it
#          instead, and a note is required
# max_ulp is what THIS project claims, in units of the last place of the
# 64-bit mantissa, against MPFR's correctly rounded answer. 0.5 would be
# correct rounding. A row above 1 says the implementation composes hardware
# instructions rather than being one, and the note says which composition
